thread:
Maya: Heads-up — Summit Tech needs to onboard a new model family for their POC. They want: real-time chat, streaming, and long-context KV cache. Also flagged security + KMS + data residency concerns. Can we run a quick fit check?
Devon: Thx — what's the model name / source? any HF link or weights?
Maya: They say it's an OSS LLM: "orpheus-xl" (private fork). HF ref pending, but they can share weights via private s3.
Devon: OK. Main things to check: 1) tokenization compatibility 2) kv-cache format (we support standard causal KV) 3) quantization/variants (we can host int8/q4_kv variants) 4) streaming + function-calling hooks.
Li: If they supply weights we can run our variant-compat scan and a quick load test. For orpheus-xl we should check rotary vs ALiBi attention, and whether the checkpoint uses grouped query attention — those impact kernel selection.
Samira: Pricing Q: customer asked delta between Hosted vs Dedicated for this model. They care about predictable latencies for SLA. Any ballpark impact if we recommend q4_kv vs fp16?
Li: Rough ballpark: fp16 on H100 -> baseline latency 60-90ms/token for 2k context. q4_kv reduces cost ~2.2x but may increase latency slightly due to dequant path, +10-20ms/token. Dedicated reserved H100s give predictable p95; hosted may route to cheaper variants under load.
Devon: Suggest we do this: 1) ask Summit to upload weights to a secure s3 link 2) run compatibility scan (tokenizer + attention pattern) 3) produce a catalog variant recommendation (fp16, q4_kv, int8 if supported) 4) run a small canary on Dedicated for 24–48h perf numbers.
Maya: I'll request s3 link and security posture info (SOC2, KMS strategy, residency). They also have an internal infosec questionnaire we need to answer — mostly on model data exfil / key management / audit logs.
Samira: For commercial, if they commit to a 6mo dedicated reserve, we can give a pricing tier that covers the reserved capacity + a model onboarding fee for compatibility testing. Need numbers from infra team.
Devon: I can produce a lightweight compatibility matrix to share with Summit: inputs: model_id, attention_type, tokenizer_name, weight_format, recommended_variants, expected perf on H100/A100.
Li: I'll pre-run a few synthetic runs against a similar open model (orpheus-mini) to get baseline numbers while we wait for weights. Helps estimate.
Maya: Summit asked about KV cache correctness for long sessions (50k tokens). Is that something we guarantee?
Devon: We support sharded KV across requests and continuous caching for prefix reuse. For 50k tokens we need to confirm sequence-split behavior and memory footprint. Will flag as potential infra limit; can require dedicated larger GPUs or batching policy adjustments.
InfrastructureBot: deploybot created checklist #onboard-231234 for model onboarding (steps: ingest weights -> compat-scan -> variant-build -> canary -> certs/KMS review).
Maya: Nice. Can we add an infosec owner to the checklist? Summit wants a single point for questionnaire follow-up.
Samira: @Devon — can you own the compatibility doc? I'll own pricing and commercial. @Li can you own perf numbers?
Devon: Yep, I'll produce the comp doc by EOD tomorrow.
Li: I'll run synthetic perf tests today and post results here.
Maya: I'll ping Summit for the s3 link + questionnaire. Also tagging legal for the data residency clause.
Samira: One more ask — Summit wants a sample API curl showing streaming + function-calls with the recommended variant. Can we include that in the handoff?
Devon: Sure, sample snippet below — we can adapt once we pick model_id:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY'
  -d '{"model":"orpheus-xl-q4_kv","stream":true,"input":"Summit: test chat"}'
```
Samira: Perfect.
Maya: Thanks team — I'll update Summit that we're starting onboarding and will share timeline once comp scan is done. :rocket:
